quantity.quote: The telescope infrastructure consisted of 12 flexible detector lines, holding photomultiplier tubes in glass spheres.
The construction for the 0.02 km³-scale detector started in 2006 and was completed in 2008.

physics_goals.quote: The ANTARES detector was the first neutrino telescope in seawater, operating successfully in the Mediterranean Sea for more than a decade and a half ... The last ANTARES published results [52] combined both the track and shower channels to search for cosmic neutrino sources.
physics_goals.value: Detect high-energy cosmic neutrinos and search for their astrophysical sources in the Mediterranean Sea

summary.plain: The first neutrino telescope built under the sea. For sixteen years, twelve long cables of light sensors hung nearly 2.5 kilometres deep in the Mediterranean off Toulon, France, watching for the faint blue flashes that a neutrino from space can make.
summary.technical: First-generation undersea Cherenkov neutrino telescope: 885 optical modules on 12 lines, 2475 m depth, 40 km offshore from Toulon, France; ~0.02 km³ instrumented volume. Collaboration formed 1996; first line deployed 2006-02-14; full 12-line detector completed 2008-05-29; switched off 2022-02-12 after nearly 16 years of continuous data taking. Predecessor experience for KM3NeT/ORCA at the same site.

unique_capabilities.quote: The ANTARES detector was the first neutrino telescope in seawater, operating successfully in the Mediterranean Sea for more than a decade and a half.
unique_capabilities.value: The first neutrino telescope built in seawater, pioneering deep-sea deployment, calibration and long-term operation techniques later used by KM3NeT
